SOURCE: "Self Improvement via Fast Tree-search" (SIFT, Recursive Self-Improvement via Fast Tree-search). Xinghong Fu (MIT), Aravinth Kulanthaivelu, Yutaro Yamada (Sakana AI). arXiv 2609.19526v1 [cs.AI], dated 17 Sep 2026. Venue: preprint. First author + date: Fu, Sept 2026.
COVERAGE: 24 of 24 pages, 78,023 chars, including appendices A and B (SWE-bench, hyperparameters, judge prompt, proofs, algorithm, discovered-agent diffs). Only the reference list (about pp. 12-14) was skimmed. Figure images not viewed; figure content comes from extracted text and captions.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. SIFT puts a cheap pairwise LLM judge in front of expensive benchmark evaluation. Judge wins and losses are fit with a regularized Bradley-Terry (BT) model, and the BT ranks drive parent sampling in a disaggregated tree search.
 number: none
 setup: built on the DGM harness. Compared with SICA, DGM and HGM on coding benchmarks.
 quote: "Expensive downstream task evaluations are reserved only for the most promising nodes."
 where: abstract, p.1
2. On full Polyglot-225 with Qwen3-Coder-30B as the coding model, SIFT beats the baselines at lower compute.
 number: SIFT 31.1% (Qwen3-480B judge) and 32.0% (gpt-5.4 judge) vs HGM 30.5%, DGM 27.1%, SICA 25.1%, base 20.0%
 setup: 30 expansion steps. Qwen3-480B is the expansion model. HGM comparison is from Wang et al. 2025. Single runs.
 quote: "the best found node achieves an accuracy of 31.1% after a total of 34.3USD in API cost and a wall clock time of 6.71h with a total of 224 CPU hours, a tenth of that of the baseline of DGM." and "HGM which reaches 30.5% accuracy at 347 CPU hours"
 where: Sec 4.1 and Table 2, p.6-7
3. With o3-mini as the coding model, SIFT reaches 35.1% against DGM's 30.7% after 80 nodes.
 number: 35.1%; three more repeats range 32.0%-35.6%; 42 CPU hours; $150; under 5 h
 setup: DGM initial harness, gpt-5-mini self-improvement model, gpt-5.4 judge, 30 steps. Table 3 lists the o3-mini/gpt-5.4 run as 20 expansion steps, $86.8, 59 CPU-h, 2.1 h, which conflicts with the 42 CPU-h figure in the text. Table 2 also lists SIFT with gpt-5-mini as judge at 31.6%, and a row "SIFT o3-mini, judge None" at 29.8%.
 quote: "we achieve an improvement to 35.1% within 30 steps of expansion, exceeding the 30.7% result obtained by DGM after 80 nodes of tree search."
 where: p.6, Table 2, Table 3
4. Evaluation is the cost bottleneck, and judging is far cheaper.
 number: Polyglot-50 full eval $6.0 and 2.6 CPU-h. Expansion $0.12 and 0.186 CPU-h. One judge call $0.044 and 0.0042 CPU-h (gpt-5.4). Up to K=10 judge calls per node. DGM-style cost cited as upward of $22,000 on SWE-Bench.
 setup: Table 1, per-task averages across 50 tasks.
 quote: "LLM-judge (pairwise call)gpt-5.40.044 0.0042 / Polyglot-50 full evalo3-mini6.0 2.6"
 where: Table 1, p.5
5. TerminalBench: the judge-selected agent beat the accuracy-selected agents under repeated full evaluation. The judge-selected agent scored lower on the search subset.
 number: judge rank 1: 32.7/89 (36.7%), search 18/50. Accuracy rank 1: 25.0/89 (28.1%), search 19/50. No-judge accuracy rank 1: 26.0/89 (29.2%). Start: 29.2%.
 setup: gpt-5-mini coding model, gpt-5 self-improvement model, gpt-5.4-high judge. 50-task search subset, 30 expansions, three repeat full evals per agent, one search run per condition.
 quote: "SIFT with judge Judge rank 1 18/50 32.7/89 (36.7%)"
 where: Table 4, p.8
6. The judge's ranking is informative but imperfect.
 number: Spearman rho 0.72, per-verdict agreement 63.2%. Judge-rank groups of 5 nodes score 28.7 / 25.0 / 21.4 / 20.2 tasks of 89, from highest to lowest rank group.
 setup: fully evaluated nodes of one TerminalBench judge-guided run.
 quote: "Spearman ρ = 0.72 / per-verdict agreement = 63.2%"
 where: Fig 5, p.8
7. A weaker judge keeps most of the global ranking signal but fails at the top of the ranking.
 number: gpt-5: rho 0.71, best agent 34.5% (+5.3), recall@5 3/5, top-5 pairwise agreement 0.50. gpt-5.4-high: rho 0.72, 36.7% (+7.5), 4/5, 1.00.
 setup: TerminalBench, 20 fully evaluated candidates per run, one run per condition.
 quote: "gpt-5.4-high36.7% +7.5 4/5 +0.72 1.00 / gpt-534.5% +5.3 3/5 +0.71 0.50"
 where: Table 5, p.9. The authors suggest a tiered setup: a cheap judge for bulk comparisons and a strong judge for the frontier.
8. Judge input format matters: full files beat diffs.
 number: Spearman 0.40 (diffs), 0.43 (diffs + swap), 0.68 (full files), 0.67 (full files + swap). Cost per comparison $0.0076 / $0.014 / $0.011 / $0.021.
 setup: Qwen3-Coder-480B judge, 50 non-root nodes from the Qwen3-30B Polyglot run. Swap-order means judging each pair in both presentation orders.
 quote: "Full files+0.45+0.680.011"
 where: Table 6, p.10
9. Most of the speedup comes from the asynchronous pipeline. Speculative expansion of judged but unevaluated nodes adds a further gain.
 number: none stated in text; read the size from Fig 6
 setup: averaged over five runs
 quote: "the asynchronous pipeline accounts for majority of the speedups"
 where: Fig 6, p.9
10. SWE-60 (SWE-bench Verified subset): judge-guided search beats the no-judge ablation.
 number: pooled 52.1% vs 47.5%, from a 40.0% start. Judge nodes repeat at 50.4% and 53.8%. No-judge nodes repeat at 44.6% and 50.4%.
 setup: gpt-5-mini coding model, gpt-5 self-improvement model, gpt-5.4-high judge, 800-evaluation budget. Four evals per agent, one run per condition.
 quote: "52.1% 47.5% starting agent: 40.0%"
 where: Fig 8, Table 7, App A, p.15
11. Harness improvements transfer to other coding models. The paper gives the direction only, with no numbers in the text.
 number: none
 setup: SIFT-found o3-mini and Qwen3 harnesses re-run with gpt-5-mini and gpt-5.4-mini
 quote: "the SIFT-discovered harnesses consistently improve Polyglot performance."
 where: Fig 4, p.7
12. Exploration term matters: with η=0 the o3-mini run reached 30.1% against 35.1% with η=1. Defaults are α=β=η=1.
 number: 30.1% vs 35.1%
 setup: o3-mini Polyglot
 quote: "with η= 0 , the lack of sufficient exploration within the tree search process leads to a reduced performance, reaching 30.1% on Polyglot (as opposed to 35.1% with η= 1 )"
 where: B.1, p.15-16
13. The judge catches faults that benchmark scores miss.
 number: BT 2.81 for node 17 (low accuracy) whose descendant node 25 reached 42%.
 setup: Polyglot-50 Qwen3 run (Fig 7); TerminalBench judge caught a flag-gated verifier "likely does nothing" and a shell rewrite that was a "major runtime risk"
 quote: "node 17, which is ranked lower in terms of accuracy, over other existing nodes, achives the highest BT judge score of 2.81"
 where: Sec 4.3, p.9
14. The discovered gains can be small edits. Node 9 reached 0.44 on the subset and 35.6% on full Polyglot from a one-line prompt edit plus a test_runner tool. Child node 24 added a larger test_analyzer and scored 33.8%.
 number: 35.6% vs 33.8%
 setup: o3-mini lineage
 quote: "the full Polyglot accuracies of node 9 and node 24 are 35.6% and 33.8% respectively"
 where: B.5, p.23

METHOD NOTES
- Parent sampling: P(i) ∝ exp(−α·r_b(i) − β·r_a(i) − η·log(1+v_i)). BT rank r_b, accuracy rank r_a, visit count v_i (Eq 1, p.3).
- Comparison targets: top 10 archive nodes. Each node is first gated on an easy subset, 4 tasks. Unevaluated nodes inherit their parent's accuracy.
- Evaluation priority queue is sorted by r_b + r_a.
- Judge sees no benchmark outputs. It receives the full patched files with a JSON reasoning-first ranking prompt (B.2).
- Theory (B.4): the regularized BT objective has a unique maximizer; the top-K recovery theorem is explicitly idealized; the rank-based sampling proposition is P(topM)=(1−e^{−αM})/(1−e^{−αn}).

LIMITS (authors' own)
- It still needs downstream benchmarks to validate. The judge is stronger than the coding model, so this is not pure self-judging.
- BT assumes a single scalar strength per node, which hides task-specific trade-offs.
- Safety: patches relaxed the evaluation harness (timeouts, retries). The authors block this by sandboxing, an allow-list of editable files, and rejecting patches that touch harness code. None got into the final experiments.
- The judge is biased toward conservative changes.
- Not shown (my read): almost all results are single search runs with no variance. The only repeats are the o3-mini range and the 3-4 repeat evals per agent. The DGM baseline uses gpt-5-mini in place of the deprecated Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Terminal Bench "2.1" is the paper's own label.
- Table 2's "judge None" rows and the cost figures in Table 3 versus the text are inconsistent (see claim 3).

BUILDS ON: Gödel Machine (Schmidhuber 2006); Gödel Agent (Yin et al. 2025); SICA (Robeyns et al. 2025); STOP (Zelikman et al. 2024); Darwin-Gödel Machine (Zhang et al. 2025b); Huxley-Gödel Machine (Wang et al. 2025); Red Queen Gödel Machine (Iacob et al. 2026); Group Evolving-Agents (Weng et al. 2026); ADAS (Hu et al. 2025); AFlow (Zhang et al. 2025c); Bradley and Terry 1952; Zheng et al. 2023 (MT-Bench judge); Polyglot (Gauthier 2024).

CODE
- Eq. 1 (p.3), Algorithm 1 (p.22, a non-blocking master loop), the MM update for BT (p.18) and the full-file judge prompt (B.2, p.16-17) are all worth keeping. Verbatim prompt line: "Write the`reasoning`field FIRST so your critique drives the ranking".
- BT fixed-point update: γ_i ← Σ_j(W_ij+λ) / Σ_j (W_ij+W_ji+2λ)/(γ_i+γ_j), normalized so Σγ = n.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.3): pipeline plus sampling formula.
- Fig 2 (p.5): disaggregated expand/evaluate pipeline. This is the best visual for a loop shape.
- Fig 3 (p.6): evolution curve, Polyglot-50 from 16% to 38% over 30 steps. (a) shows judge calls finishing faster than a single eval.
- Fig 5 (p.8): judge rank versus realized accuracy.
- Fig 6 (p.9): speedup ablation.
- Fig 7 (p.9): tree where a low-accuracy node with the top BT score led to the best descendant.
- Fig 9 (p.16): SWE-60 lineage.

PLACEMENT: It fits note 08 (self-improving loops) as the main case. The agent edits its own harness and the key idea is cheap judge ranking in front of costly verification. It also gives note 02 a loop-shape example: tree search with an archive, plus an async disaggregated expand/evaluate pipeline. Cite it in 02 as a secondary reference. One caveat for the note: tell the reader that the judge was stronger than the coding model, and that the evidence is single runs.

PROBLEMS: Table cell text is run together in the extraction. The Table 3 / text mismatch is in the source itself. No embedded instructions found. Figure 6 has no numbers in the text.
